boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus destinations with documented study, gathering, recreation, or performance uses.

cards.title: Oesterle Library & Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: 320 E. School St. · quiet and collaborative study areas
cards.notes: Choose a quiet zone for solo work, reserve a group room when available, or meet classmates in the collaborative study areas.
cards.short_summary: A library destination with quiet, group, and collaborative study options.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central identifies Oesterle Library & Learning Commons as offering quiet zones, group study rooms, and collaborative workspaces.
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists the library at 320 E. School St.; confirm building access and room availability locally.

cards.title: Multicultural Student Center
cards.subtitle: Harold and Eva White Activities Center · Room 206
cards.notes: Use the open workspace to meet, watch television, or browse the multicultural bookshelf; check campus guidance for room access.
cards.short_summary: An inclusive collaborative room with shared media and workspace.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central describes the Multicultural Student Center as an inclusive, collaborative space with television, open workspace, and a multicultural bookshelf.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Harold and Eva White Activities Center, room 206; observe posted access rules.

cards.title: Jefferson Lounge
cards.subtitle: Seager Hall · activity space with pool table and television
cards.notes: Bring a study break or a small group to the lounge for its pool table and television, while respecting residence-hall policies.
cards.short_summary: A Seager Hall activity lounge equipped for casual downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central identifies Jefferson Lounge in Seager Hall as an activity space with a pool table and television.
cards.access_notes: Located in Seager Hall; access may be governed by residence-hall and card-access policies.

cards.title: Jefferson Commons
cards.subtitle: Outside Wentz Science Center · lawn and outdoor activity space
cards.notes: Set up an outdoor study session or meet between classes on the lawn; reserve the fire pit through the College event system if needed.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor commons for events, informal gathering, and lawn time.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central describes Jefferson Commons outside Wentz Science Center as an outdoor activity space with event lawns and a reservable fire pit.
cards.access_notes: Fire-pit use requires reservation through the College event-calendar system; follow event and weather restrictions.

cards.title: Wentz Science Center gathering spaces
cards.subtitle: 131 S. Loomis St. · eight themed gathering spaces
cards.notes: Meet classmates in one of the building’s themed gathering spaces for a shared work session, keeping labs and class activity clear.
cards.short_summary: Science building with themed spaces intended for studying with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central says Wentz Science Center is a place where students study with friends in eight themed gathering spaces.
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists Wentz Science Center at 131 S. Loomis St.; comply with posted room and lab access rules.

cards.title: Rolland Center Boilerhouse Café
cards.subtitle: 29 N. Loomis St. · “BoHo”
cards.notes: Use this campus café as a study stop or a place to meet over coffee and snacks; check current dining service before planning.
cards.short_summary: A campus café explicitly described as a place to study.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central’s campus-lingo guide defines “BoHo” as the Rolland Center Boilerhouse Café, a place to study and get coffee and snacks.
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists the Rolland Center Boilerhouse Café at 29 N. Loomis St.; food and beverages require purchase.

cards.title: Jefferson Lawn
cards.subtitle: North of Seager Hall · also called J-Lawn
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a book to the grass north of Seager Hall for a low-key outdoor study or relaxation break.
cards.short_summary: A named lawn documented as a spot for studying or relaxing.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central identifies Jefferson Lawn as the grassy area north of Seager Hall where students may study or relax.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; keep clear of scheduled campus activity and follow posted rules.

cards.title: Championship Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between Merner Field House and Benedetti-Wehrli Stadium
cards.notes: Meet friends before a home game or look for scheduled campus events in the brick plaza patio between the athletic venues.
cards.short_summary: A named plaza used for pre-game celebrations and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central identifies Championship Plaza as the brick patio between Merner Field House and Benedetti-Wehrli Stadium and notes its pre-game and campus-event use.
cards.access_notes: Located between athletic facilities; event access and activities vary with the campus schedule.

cards.title: Fort Hill Pond
cards.subtitle: Behind Patterson and Ward residence halls
cards.notes: Take a quiet outdoor pause by the pond behind Patterson and Ward, staying on permitted paths and respecting nearby residence halls.
cards.short_summary: A named campus pond in the Fort Hill residential area.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central’s campus-lingo guide identifies the Fort Hill Pond as located behind Patterson and Ward residence halls.
cards.access_notes: Near residence halls; use only public, permitted outdoor areas and observe posted safety guidance.

cards.title: Residence Hall/Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 440 S. Brainard St. · Res/Rec
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule for an open time to use the indoor track or other recreation facilities, then follow facility rules.
cards.short_summary: A combined residence and recreation complex with an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: North Central describes the Residence Hall/Recreation Center as a dual complex with a competition-size indoor track and recreation center.
cards.access_notes: Campus map lists the building at 440 S. Brainard St.; facilities are available when not occupied by scheduled events.
